metadata.purpose: Educational modules and worked examples, sourced from the pricing registries and official GitHub billing documentation.

apiStrategies.title: Route by workload
apiStrategies.body: Use a lower-cost model for classification, extraction and short summaries; reserve higher-cost reasoning for cases that need it.

apiStrategies.title: Control output budget
apiStrategies.body: Output tokens are often materially more expensive than input tokens. Ask for precise structures and bounded response sizes.

apiStrategies.title: Reuse stable context
apiStrategies.body: When a provider supports caching, repeated instructions or reference context may be billed at a lower cached-input rate.

apiStrategies.title: Use async pricing modes
apiStrategies.body: For non-urgent processing, compare verified Batch or Flex modes when available in official provider pricing.

apiStrategies.title: Watch threshold pricing
apiStrategies.body: Very large prompts can cross documented pricing tiers. A single context expansion can change the unit economics.

apiStrategies.title: Validate quality, not price alone
apiStrategies.body: Cost reduction is useful only if accuracy, safety, latency and output usability remain acceptable.

copilotStrategies.title: Start with no-credit features
copilotStrategies.body: On paid Copilot plans, code completions and next edit suggestions are not billed in AI credits. Use chat or agent workflows only when the task needs them.

copilotStrategies.title: Use Auto where appropriate
copilotStrategies.body: For eligible paid-plan Chat, CLI and cloud-agent use, GitHub documents a 10% model-cost discount. Auto is optimized for task fit, reliability and availability—not merely the cheapest model.

copilotStrategies.title: Trim the context you send
copilotStrategies.body: Limit the files, chat history and instructions included in an interaction. Input volume directly influences token-based cost.

copilotStrategies.title: Preserve useful cached context
copilotStrategies.body: Cached-token pricing is lower than fresh input for published Copilot models. Avoid unnecessary session switching when it causes useful context to be rebuilt.

copilotStrategies.title: Choose lighter models for routine work
copilotStrategies.body: Simple explanations, small edits and predictable transformations often do not require frontier-model pricing.

copilotStrategies.title: Break down agentic tasks
copilotStrategies.body: Cloud-agent and multi-step workflows can involve multiple model calls. Narrow task boundaries make assumptions and spending easier to control.

copilotStrategies.title: Minimize unused tool context
copilotStrategies.body: Where tools or MCP schemas are included in the model context, unnecessary tool exposure can increase input volume. Treat this as an optimization hypothesis and verify with usage data.

copilotStrategies.title: Set budgets before overage
copilotStrategies.body: GitHub supports budget controls. Business and Enterprise pools can be exhausted by heavy users, and there is no automatic fallback to cheaper models when budgets are exhausted.
